page: Amazon Web Services r7g.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton3 processor family. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a nominal clock frequency of 2.6 GHz using the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is supported via native AES instructions, while x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX and AMX are absent.

System memory totals 32.0 GB, delivering an 8.0 GB per-core allocation suited for memory-intensive architectures. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage and has no hardware accelerators or GPUs. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Synthetic testing reflects strong memory subsystem performance, characterized by a PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25 percent and measured uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 97.0 GB/sec. Application benchmarks show balanced throughput, recording 6.63 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 8.32 GB/sec in static web serving. General integer and compilation metrics, such as Geekbench multi-core at 4847.0 and Clang compilation at 6257.0, fall within the middle 50 percent of tested cloud servers. Conversely, floating-point intensive tasks, extended instruction suites, and local CPU-based LLM inference exhibit lower relative throughput, with PassMark CPU encryption ranking in the lowest 10 percent.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides dense memory capacity per core on power-efficient arm64 silicon. The r7g.xlarge is tailored for caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, relational and key-value datastores with moderate query complexity, in-memory data processing, and back-end application runtimes requiring high memory headroom rather than heavy vector compute.

The instance delivers 32.0 GB of memory at an 8.0 GB per-core ratio, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache and running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It contains no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators, paired with a baseline network speed of 2 Gbps. Empirical benchmarks indicate strong memory subsystem throughput, with PassMark memory ranking in the upper quartile and Redis handling 6.63 million SET operations per second. General compute performance in Geekbench and web serving remains balanced, though CPU-bound encryption and AI inference rank lower relative to x86 alternatives with dedicated vector extensions. The instance profile is tailored for memory-intensive deployments including in-memory datastores, caching tiers, and medium-scale transactional backend databases.
